s: the market hall famous for a 300-gram mortadella sandwich
w: São Paulo's grand 1933 municipal market, its stained-glass windows lit up over stalls of fruit and produce, is best known now for one specific ritual: the mortadella sandwich at Hocca, founded here in 1952 by Portuguese immigrants -- some 300 grams of mortadella, about 13 slices, stacked into a single bun. Four Hocca counters inside the market keep the queue moving.
_facts: Located at Rua da Cantareira 306, Centro, São Paulo
Market building opened in 1933, known for stained-glass windows
Home to Hocca, founded 1952, famous for its ~300g mortadella sandwich
Four Hocca stalls operate inside the market

s: a specialty coffee bar in the courtyard garden of a four-storey bookshop
w: Tucked behind Livraria da Vila, a four-floor Vila Madalena bookshop, this café sits in a courtyard shaded by jabuticaba and mulberry trees -- browse the shelves, then take gourmet coffee, açaí bowls or avocado toast out into the garden. A quieter, more literary note in a neighbourhood better known for its bars and street art.
_facts: Located at Rua Fradique Coutinho 915, Vila Madalena, São Paulo
Café set inside/behind Livraria da Vila, a four-floor bookshop
Courtyard seating shaded by jabuticaba and mulberry trees
Known for gourmet coffee and brunch dishes (açaí bowls, avocado toast)

s: a kissaten-style coffee bar built on a composer's move into roasting
w: Founded by former composer Tiago de Mello and his wife, pastry chef Larissa Taketa, after coffee-and-pastry research trips through Tokyo, Taipei and Seoul -- the resulting kissaten-style bar treats brewing with the same precision as musical composition. Single-origin coffees with notes of yuzu, magnolia or fig sit alongside pão de queijo and Asian-inflected pastries.
_facts: Located at Rua Ferreira de Araújo 353, Pinheiros, São Paulo
Founded by Tiago de Mello (formerly a music composer) and pastry chef Larissa Taketa
Concept shaped by coffee and pastry research trips to Tokyo, Taipei and Seoul
Known for single-origin coffees and Asian-influenced pastries alongside pão de queijo

s: a cycling-themed café since 2014, coffee and homemade bread for riders and regulars
w: A cycling-themed café in Pinheiros open since 2014, equal parts coffee bar and clubhouse for the city's road and gravel riders -- homemade bread, cookies and specialty coffee alongside bike accessories for sale. Welcoming to anyone, but built around the rhythm of a pre- or post-ride stop.
_facts: Located at Rua Artur de Azevedo 1317, Pinheiros, São Paulo
Cycling-themed café established in 2014
Known for specialty coffee, homemade bread and cookies
Also sells cycling accessories

s: a hillside garden restaurant serving organic Brazilian cuisine above the city
w: A restaurant built into a hillside garden in bohemian Santa Teresa, its open-air pavilions looking out over Rio below. Chef Ana Castilho works organic and biodynamic ingredients sourced from across Brazil into a menu of refined, ingredient-forward Brazilian dishes, recognised in the Michelin Guide.
_facts: Located at Rua Aprazível 62, Santa Teresa, Rio de Janeiro
Open-air restaurant set in a hillside garden
Run by chef Ana Castilho, using organic and biodynamic Brazilian ingredients
Listed in the Michelin Guide Brazil

s: a 1957 Portuguese tapas bar with wine jugs stacked to the ceiling
w: A Portuguese tapas bar founded in 1957 by a family from Madeira, wine jugs lining shelves that reach the ceiling and around a hundred tapas stewing behind the glass counter. Tucked on a Copacabana side street across from the metro, it's stayed a local standby for standing-room tapas and wine rather than chasing the beachfront crowd.
_facts: Located at Rua Siqueira Campos 138, Copacabana, Rio de Janeiro
Founded in 1957 by a Portuguese family from Madeira
Portuguese-style tapas bar (petiscos) with wine served from jugs
Located across from Siqueira Campos metro station
